issue.title: Bring harness + per-task model dispatch (OpenCode/OpenRouter) to Harbour
issue.description:
## Why

Simple Dispatcher (SD) now has a working, fully-tested `opencode` harness (LIN-1077, parent LIN-393) alongside its default `claude-code` harness — a dispatched task can run through OpenCode against any OpenRouter-backed model instead of Claude Code. This unlocks materially cheaper models for tasks that don't need Claude Code's full capability, with SD's own receiving end already proven end-to-end: a live dispatch item carrying `harness: "opencode"` + `model: "openrouter/<provider-model>"` was run through SD's real admission/routing/launch pipeline (real per-session `opencode serve`, real OpenRouter model call, real completion reaper) and completed successfully.

What's missing is on Harbour's side: there is currently no way for whatever produces a dispatch (Harbour's own UI/API/automation) to actually SET these fields end-to-end. LIN-1077's own research flagged this as an open cross-repo question: the dispatch-creation proxy currently documents forwarding `model` but not `harness` at all, so even if a caller wanted to request OpenCode today, there's no path for that field to survive from Harbour into SD's queue payload.

## What this covers

1. **Forward** `harness` **end-to-end.** Confirm/fix the dispatch-creation proxy so a `harness` field set on a dispatch request actually reaches SD's queue item (mirroring how `model` is already forwarded, per SD's existing `item.model` read).
2. **Surface harness + model selection** wherever dispatches are created/configured on the Harbour side (UI and/or API/automation surface) — so a user or an automated flow can deliberately pick `opencode` + a specific OpenRouter model for a task, not just accept the `claude-code` default.
3. **Precedence parity.** SD resolves `harness`/`model` on a payload > per-workspace-default > global-default chain (`harnesses.js`'s `resolveHarness`/`resolveModel`); confirm Harbour's UI/API exposes (or deliberately omits) the equivalent per-workspace default concept, so the two systems' defaulting behavior doesn't silently diverge.
4. **Follow-up/resume awareness.** OpenCode follow-ups continue via a real, opencode-native session id SD persists internally (there is no CLI/API way to assign a custom session id up front) — this is entirely internal to SD and needs no Harbour-side change, but is worth noting so a Harbour-side "resume this dispatch" flow doesn't assume the same resume mechanics as `claude-code`.

## Out of scope

* Any further SD-side harness work (that's tracked in the Simple Dispatcher project, LIN-393/LIN-1077 and their descendants).
* The Codex CLI harness (separate, hook-alignment work, tracked separately per LIN-393's research thread).

## References

* LIN-1077 (Simple Dispatcher): the OpenCode harness implementation, including the server-per-session redesign and its full test coverage (unit, real-subprocess, and real-binary e2e including mid-task abort/teardown).
* LIN-393 (Simple Dispatcher, parent): the original pluggable-engine research thread that first flagged this Harbour-side gap.

## Implementation Plan

(Full evidence trail in the Linear comments — 4-beat planning pass. Summary below.)

### Fork decisions

* **Fork A — API/proxy-only now, UI deferred.** `model` (LIN-438) shipped with zero Dispatch-page UI exposure for its whole life without that being a treated gap, and the ticket wording ("UI **and/or** API/automation surface") treats these as alternatives. Wire `harness` through the API/proxy layer only; file a separate follow-up ticket for a Dispatch-page harness dropdown + model input.
* **Fork B — extract a shared validator.** A confirmed live divergence exists between `routes/proxy.js:4242` and `routes/dispatch.js:310`'s independently-written `model` validation (`model: 0` is rejected by one, silently accepted by the other). Rather than hand-duplicating a second field (`harness`) the same drift-prone way, extract a small shared opaque-field validator used by both routers for both fields — fixes the existing bug as a side effect.

### File-by-file plan, in dependency order

1. **New** `lib/dispatch-validation.js` — `validateOpaqueDispatchField(value, fieldName, { maxLength })`: the type/length/`DANGEROUS_CHARS_REGEX` check currently duplicated (with drift) at `routes/proxy.js:4242-4266` and `routes/dispatch.js:305-331`.
2. `lib/dispatch-store.js` (the load-bearing seam — land before the routers): `addItem` (`:138`, JSDoc `:126`) stores `harness: item.harness || null` beside `model` (`:171`); `_formatItem` (`:948`) forwards `harness: doc.harness || null` beside `:969` (this is the line the external runner's poll/take actually reads); archive/history path (`:517`) gets the same sibling field; schema comment (`:21`) gets a `harness` line.
3. `routes/proxy.js`: `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` (`:4135`) — destructure `harness` (`:4142`), validate via the shared helper, forward (`:4394`). `POST /api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` (`:4451`) — destructure, validate, forward at **both** call sites `:4600` and `:4741` (easy to miss one). `formatDispatchWatch` (`:445-478`) intentionally left NOT echoing `harness`/`model` — matches existing `model` behavior, not new scope. Update embedded `/api/proxy/instructions` text (`:1240-1257`) for `harness`. Wording fix at `:1272` — drop the literal "cold claude --resume" for generic phrasing (per the follow-up/resume-awareness check — this line will become inaccurate once opencode follow-ups exist).
4. `routes/dispatch.js`: `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` (`:199`) — destructure, validate via shared helper, forward (`:413`).
5. `docs/dispatch-integration.md`: new `harness` field-table row (`:279`) + a "Harness (`harness`)" section mirroring "Execution model (`model`)" (`:499-533`) — opaque, forwarded blindly, `null`/omit preserves SD's own default, and explicitly note Harbour does NOT interpose a per-workspace default (see Precedence below).
6. **Deferred to a follow-up ticket**: `public/dispatch.js` + `lib/render-dispatch.js` UI control (harness dropdown + model input).

Order: **validator → store → proxy router → user-dispatch router → docs.** Store has no dependency on the routers and must land first since both routers forward into it.

### Precedence/defaulting

Confirmed no existing per-workspace-default layer for the dispatch execution model/harness (`resolveWorkspaceModel` in `lib/workspace-preferences.js:136` is a real per-workspace default, but for the unrelated *generation* model used by recommend/recap/brief/etc., never called from the dispatch-creation path). Keep the two-tier shape: **dispatch payload value → null → SD's own precedence chain** — do not add a new Harbour-side default tier; SD already owns that resolution.

### Testing strategy

Mirror and extend the three existing `model`-forwarding unit test files (add `harness` alongside `model` in each, same fixtures/pattern):

* `tests/unit/dispatch-store-model.test.js` — store-level `addItem`/`_formatItem`/archive forwarding.
* `tests/unit/dispatch-route-model.test.js` — `routes/dispatch.js` accept/validate/forward.
* `tests/unit/proxy-dispatch-model.test.js` — `routes/proxy.js`, both endpoints, both `recommend-and-dispatch` call sites.
* New: unit tests for `lib/dispatch-validation.js` (length/dangerous-chars cases) plus a regression test pinning the fixed `model: 0` behavior (now consistent across both routers).
* No E2E this pass — the only user-facing surface (UI) is deferred to the follow-up ticket; mirrors how `model`/LIN-438 itself shipped (unit-only, no UI, no E2E).

## Session Fit

One focused implementation session — the wiring is mechanical, precisely file:line-mapped (6 files, ~8 call sites), both forks are decided above, and there are no open research/design questions left. The Dispatch-page UI control is explicitly out of this session and belongs to its own follow-up ticket.

## Beat 1/4 — Survey: staleness check + surface inventory

### Staleness check

`git log --since="2026-07-06T07:35:06.183Z"` against every file this ticket references (`routes/proxy.js`, `routes/dispatch.js`, `lib/dispatch-store.js`, `lib/dispatch-tokens.js`, `public/dispatch.js`, `lib/render-dispatch.js`, `lib/harbour-spawn.js`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md`) returns **no commits** — nothing has changed since the ticket was created today. Re-read at HEAD confirms the ticket's central claim: **`model` is forwarded end-to-end; `harness` does not exist anywhere in the dispatch pipeline.** Not a single hit for `harness` in any of those files (the lone grep hit, `routes/proxy.js:308`, is an unrelated code comment referencing the test fixture file name `local-harness.js`).

### Surface inventory (today's behavior, cited)

**1. `routes/proxy.js` — consumer-facing proxy dispatch endpoints (this session's own substrate)**
- `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` (`routes/proxy.js:4135`): destructures `model` from `req.body` at `:4142` (no `harness` in the destructure). Validates `model` as an opaque string — type/length/dangerous-chars checks at `:4242-4266`. Forwards it into `dispatchQueueStore.addItem(...)` as `model: model || null` at `:4394`. No `harness` field is read, validated, or forwarded anywhere in the handler.
- `POST /api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` (`routes/proxy.js:4451`): same pattern — `model` destructured at `:4451`, validated `:4493-4498`, forwarded `:4600` and `:4741` (two call sites: direct dispatch + override-verb path). No `harness`.
- The endpoint's own self-documentation (the `/api/proxy/instructions` text embedded at `:1240-1257`) documents `model` in detail ("EXECUTION model the runner should use to RUN this prompt", OpenRouter `provider/model` convention) and says nothing about `harness` — confirms the ticket's claim that the proxy documents `model` forwarding but is silent on `harness`.

**2. `routes/dispatch.js` — user-facing session-authed dispatch API**
- `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` (`routes/dispatch.js:199`): identical shape — `model` destructured at `:199`, validated `:305-331` (mirrors the proxy path's opaque-string checks), forwarded as `model: model || null` at `:413`. No `harness` anywhere in this file.

**3. `lib/dispatch-store.js` — the shared persistence/forwarding seam both routes call into**
- `addItem(urlKey, item)` (`:138`): JSDoc at `:126` documents `item.model` as "Execution model … opaque, not registry-validated … stored + forwarded blindly." Stores it as `model: item.model || null` at `:171`. No `harness` field in the schema or JSDoc.
- `_formatItem(doc)` (`:948`) — the function that shapes the poll/take response the external runner actually reads — forwards `model: doc.model || null` at `:969`, annotated "The load-bearing forward for LIN-438: deliver the execution model so the external runner can pass it to its own CLI." This is the exact seam SD's `item.model` read pulls from; a `harness` sibling would need to land here too. Currently absent.
- The archive/history path (`:517`, inside the take/resolve flow) also forwards `model: doc.model || null` with no `harness` counterpart.
- **`lib/dispatch-tokens.js`**: no `model`/`harness` concept at all — it only handles token creation/listing/hashing/revocation, not dispatch item fields. Not a relevant surface for this ticket.

**4. `public/dispatch.js` + `lib/render-dispatch.js` — the human Dispatch page UI**
- Zero occurrences of `model` or `harness` in either file. The rendered UI (`lib/render-dispatch.js:57-88`) exposes exactly: a prompt textarea, a repo `<select>`, and target buttons (`cli`/`web`/`dash`/`local`-when-localhost) plus a `+proxy` toggle. **There is no model selector on the Dispatch page today, let alone a harness selector** — model/harness selection currently exists only as API/proxy fields, never as a UI control. This is a surface the ticket's item 2 ("surface harness + model selection … UI and/or API") will need to address if UI exposure is in scope.

**5. `lib/harbour-spawn.js` — local/Harbour OS dispatch target**
- Zero occurrences of `model` or `harness`. Confirms the ticket's own scoping note: local target is out of scope since SD dispatch consumers are the cli/web targets, and this file has no model/harness concept to extend regardless.

**6. `docs/dispatch-integration.md` — consumer integration guide**
- Documents `model` thoroughly: field table entry at `:279`, and a full "Execution model (`model`)" section at `:499-533` covering wire convention, opacity, and the model ≠ generation-model distinction. Zero mentions of `harness` anywhere in the doc — the integration guide will need a new section once `harness` forwarding exists.

### Summary of the gap

The forwarding gap is real and precisely bounded: `model` flows cleanly through three layers — `routes/proxy.js` (consumer) / `routes/dispatch.js` (user) → `lib/dispatch-store.js addItem` (persist) → `lib/dispatch-store.js _formatItem` (poll/take response the runner reads) — with validation, JSDoc, and docs all in place. `harness` has **no presence at any of those layers**, and no UI surface exposes either field today (the Dispatch page has no model or harness control). Next beat can use this as the exact map of files/functions/line-anchors to patch (validate → store → forward) plus the UI/docs surfaces that need new affordances, without needing to re-derive today's `model` plumbing from scratch.

## Beat 2/4 — Cross-cutting concerns + precedence/defaulting

### 1. Cross-cutting interaction map: every layer that must move together

A `harness` field mirrors `model`'s existing plumbing, so it must be threaded into the SAME set of layers `model` already touches. Missing any one of these silently breaks end-to-end forwarding — exactly the failure mode the ticket describes for `harness` today.

| Layer | File:line | Role | harness would need |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proxy dispatch | `routes/proxy.js:4142` (destructure), `:4242-4266` (validate), `:4394` (forward into `addItem`) | Consumer-facing `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` | Same 3 steps |
| Proxy recommend-and-dispatch | `routes/proxy.js:4451` (destructure), `:4493-4498` (validate), `:4600` AND `:4741` (TWO separate `addItem` call sites — direct-dispatch branch and the override-verb branch) | Fused recommend+dispatch verb | Same steps, at BOTH forward call sites — missing either one leaves override-verb dispatches silently harness-less while direct dispatches work |
| User dispatch API | `routes/dispatch.js:199` (destructure), `:305-331` (validate), `:413` (forward into `addItem`) | Session-authed `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` | Same 3 steps, independently (see divergence risk below) |
| Store: persist | `lib/dispatch-store.js:126` (JSDoc), `:138` (`addItem` signature), `:171` (`model: item.model \|\| null` store) | Shared persistence seam both routers call into | New `harness` schema field + JSDoc entry |
| Store: runner-facing forward | `lib/dispatch-store.js:948` (`_formatItem`), `:969` (`model: doc.model \|\| null`) | Shapes the poll/take response the EXTERNAL RUNNER reads — this is the actual seam SD's `item.model` (and would-be `item.harness`) read pulls from | New `harness: doc.harness \|\| null` forward — this is the single most load-bearing line; everything upstream is inert until this line exists |
| Store: archive/history | `lib/dispatch-store.js:517` (inside the take/resolve archive path) | Secondary forward into the history doc (feeds dispatch history reads / Observation) | Same sibling field |
| Docs | `docs/dispatch-integration.md:279` (field table), `:499-533` (dedicated "Execution model" section) | Consumer integration guide | New parallel `harness` field-table row + section, or the guide silently under-documents a live field (as it currently does for `harness`) |

**Confirmed existing divergence — proof this duplication already drifts without a shared helper.** `routes/proxy.js:4242` validates model presence as `model !== undefined && model !== null && typeof model !== 'string'`, while `routes/dispatch.js:310` validates it as `if (model && typeof model !== 'string')`. These are NOT equivalent: a payload of `model: 0` (or any falsy-but-non-string value) is REJECTED by the proxy path (`0 !== undefined && 0 !== null` is true, `typeof 0 !== 'string'` is true → 400) but SILENTLY ACCEPTED as absent by the user-dispatch path (`0 &&` short-circuits false → no error, then `model \|\| null` treats it as null downstream). This is a live, present-day inconsistency between the two independently-written validation blocks — not hypothetical. It means: (a) a `harness` implementation must not just copy whichever block is closer at hand, it should either fix this drift while adding the parallel field, or explicitly decide to leave the two paths non-identical and document why; (b) if the plan wants byte-for-byte parity going forward, extracting a shared `validateDispatchModel`/`validateDispatchHarness`-style helper (there is currently no shared validation module between `routes/proxy.js` and `routes/dispatch.js` — each duplicates its own `MAX_NAME_LENGTH`/`DANGEROUS_CHARS_REGEX` checks inline) would remove the recurring risk rather than adding a third duplicated block.

**UI is not a cross-cutting sync risk today** — confirmed in beat 1, `public/dispatch.js`/`lib/render-dispatch.js` have no `model` field to keep in sync, so there's no existing UI state to diverge from. It becomes a sync concern only once/if beat 4's plan adds a model+harness UI control pair — at that point they'd need to be introduced together, not staggered.

### 2. Precedence/defaulting assessment

**Searched:** `lib/workspace-preferences.js`, `lib/user-preferences.js`, `lib/feature-defaults.js`, plus a repo-wide grep for `resolveWorkspaceModel` / any default-model wiring into the dispatch write path.

**Finding: Harbour DOES have a per-workspace default — but it is the wrong namespace.** `lib/workspace-preferences.js:136` (`resolveWorkspaceModel({ urlKey, workspacePreferencesStore, forceDefault })`) resolves a per-workspace default model from `prefs.modelId` (falling back to `DEFAULT_MODEL`), and it's real, live infrastructure — called from `routes/proxy.js:2920,3325,3441,3597,3712`, `routes/next-run.js:188`, `routes/task-chat.js:420`, `routes/workspace-api.js` (8 call sites: `:662,813,1108,1566,1790,2350,2578,2671,3200`), and `server.js:1696`. **But every one of those call sites is a GENERATION-model use** — recommend/recap/brief/roadmap/task-chat/next-run, i.e. the server-side LLM call that WRITES a prompt — the exact namespace the codebase's own comments repeatedly warn is distinct from the dispatch EXECUTION model (see `routes/proxy.js:1242`, `:2918` "model ≠ generation model", `docs/dispatch-integration.md:509-512`). It is also billing-sensitive: `forceDefault`/`isFreeTier` clamps it so free-tier requests never bill a workspace-preferred model (LIN-513) — a concern that has nothing to do with which harness/model an external runner uses to execute a dispatched task.

**Direct check of the dispatch-creation path itself:** zero calls to `resolveWorkspaceModel` (or any other preference lookup) appear anywhere in `routes/proxy.js`'s two dispatch endpoints (`:4135`, `:4451`) or in `routes/dispatch.js`'s dispatch endpoint (`:199` handler). The execution `model` field is written exactly once, verbatim from the request: `model: model \|\| null` (`routes/proxy.js:4394`, `:4600`, `:4741`; `routes/dispatch.js:413`). `lib/feature-defaults.js` and `lib/user-preferences.js` have zero occurrences of `model` or `harness` (confirmed by grep — no output).

**Conclusion: Harbour does NOT have a per-workspace-default layer for the dispatch execution model/harness today.** The current behavior is a strict two-tier chain: **dispatch payload value → `null` → whatever the runner/SD does with `null`** (today: "the consumer's current default," per `routes/proxy.js:1242`; under this ticket, SD's own global default in its 3-tier `resolveHarness`/`resolveModel`). There is no Harbour-side middle tier interposed, and nothing in the codebase suggests one was ever built or half-built for this purpose — `resolveWorkspaceModel` is a real per-workspace default, just for an entirely different (generation-model) concern.

**Recommendation for the next beat:** given the evidence, Harbour should **deliberately keep the two-tier shape** for `model`/`harness` on dispatch (payload > null > runner's own default) rather than introducing a new Harbour-side per-workspace-default tier. Reasons, grounded in what's actually in the codebase: (1) reusing/extending `resolveWorkspaceModel` for this would conflate two namespaces the codebase has gone out of its way, repeatedly, in comments across `routes/proxy.js`, `lib/dispatch-store.js`, and `docs/dispatch-integration.md`, to keep separate — doing so risks a free-tier-billing-clamped generation-model value leaking into an execution-model field it was never designed to represent; (2) SD already owns tiers 2–3 of the precedence chain (its own per-workspace-default and global-default, per `harnesses.js`), so Harbour introducing its OWN competing per-workspace-default tier would create two independent, unsynchronized "workspace default" concepts for the same field — the ticket's own constraint ("must not silently diverge") argues for Harbour staying a thin pass-through (payload or omit) and letting SD's existing precedence resolve the rest, not duplicating that resolution logic across two repos. If the plan later decides a Harbour-side default IS wanted (e.g. so the Dispatch UI can show/persist a per-workspace preferred harness+model), that would need to be a NEW preference key under `workspace-preferences.js` (parallel to, not reusing, `modelId`) — but nothing in today's codebase demands that; it would be new scope, not a gap-fill of an existing-but-broken layer.

Next beat can treat this as settled: no existing per-workspace-default plumbing to hook into for the execution model/harness; the design question is only whether to add one net-new, and the evidence favors not doing so.

## Beat 3/4 — Follow-up/resume awareness + solution-shape check

### 1. Follow-up/resume awareness

**Checked:** `followUpTo` handling in `routes/proxy.js` and `routes/dispatch.js`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md`'s Follow-ups section, and the reply-box flow (`public/session.js` + `lib/render-session.js`'s `renderReplyBox`).

**The mechanics themselves are already harness-agnostic — confirmed, not assumed:**
- `routes/proxy.js:4279-4288` and `routes/dispatch.js:344-350` validate `followUpTo` identically: well-formed UUID, and `target` restricted to `cli`/`web` (`dash`/`local` rejected). Neither check inspects, infers, or requires anything about the target session's harness — it's a pure UUID + target-enum check.
- `docs/dispatch-integration.md:303-304` states the invariant explicitly: "The dispatch store records and forwards `followUpTo` verbatim — it owns no session identity or liveness; the **consumer** maps `followUpTo` back to its live session." This is already written to be harness-neutral by design — Harbour never touches session identity, so nothing here would need to change to support opencode follow-ups (matching the ticket's own point 4 that OpenCode's session continuity is entirely SD-internal).
- `lib/render-session.js:140-159` (`renderReplyBox`) and `public/session.js:35-80` key purely on `sessionTerminal` (boolean) to decide whether to send `force: true` — generic wording ("no live session to resume", "reply queued"), no harness-specific language or logic anywhere in either file. **No changes needed here.**

**One real wording gap found — a Claude-Code-specific mechanic is named inside otherwise-generic prose.** `routes/proxy.js:1272` (the `/api/proxy/instructions` text — i.e. what an external consumer, including a future opencode-targeted orchestrator, actually reads to understand the API) says: *"...with the hold absent the worker finalizes after beat 1, so beat 2's followUpTo+force falls back to a cold **claude --resume** instead of an in-session warm follow-on."* This is the only spot in production docs/code that names the literal `claude --resume` CLI invocation (confirmed by repo-wide grep — the only other hits are a mirroring test comment, `tests/unit/autopilot-kickoff.test.js:372`, and a historical incident-review doc, `docs/reviews/recent-headwinds-review-2026-07-02.md:119`, which is a point-in-time postmortem and correctly describes what was literally true then). Everywhere else this same fallback concept is described generically as a **"cold `--resume`"** with no harness named — e.g. `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:127,165` (the live kickoff prompt text sent into orchestrator sessions), `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md:263`, and `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md:286,295`. Those are already harness-neutral phrasing and need no change.

**Why this matters for this ticket specifically:** once a follow-up dispatch can target an opencode session, the `waitForFollowUps`-absent fallback is NOT "a cold `claude --resume`" for that session — it's whatever SD's own opencode-native session-resume mechanism is (per the ticket's point 4, an internal SD concern Harbour has no visibility into or control over). Leaving `routes/proxy.js:1272`'s wording as-is would make Harbour's own API documentation assert an implementation detail that is false for a harness other than claude-code, which is exactly the misleading-wording risk the ticket flagged. **Recommended fix (wording-only, no behavior change):** generalize that one sentence to something like "falls back to a cold resume via the runner's own mechanism" — remove the literal `claude --resume` naming. No code/logic change is implied; `followUpTo`/`force`/`waitForFollowUps` themselves need no change, only this one doc string.

### 2. Solution-shape check — two genuine forks, neither silently resolved

**Fork A: how far to take "surface harness + model selection" (ticket item 2).**
- *Option A1 — API/proxy-only now, UI deferred.* Land the validate→store→forward wiring (per beat 2's map) so any caller that already speaks the dispatch API/proxy (an automated orchestrator, a hand-built consumer, this very autopilot session) can set `harness`+`model` today. Defer a Dispatch-page UI control to a separate follow-up. **This has direct precedent**: beat 1 confirmed `model` itself (LIN-438) has shipped with **zero UI exposure** on the Dispatch page (`public/dispatch.js` / `lib/render-dispatch.js` — no model selector exists) for its entire life, and that has not been treated as an outstanding gap. The ticket's own wording ("Surface harness + model selection … UI **and/or** API/automation surface") explicitly treats these as alternatives, not a mandatory pair.
- *Option A2 — both together in one pass.* Add a harness dropdown + model input to the Dispatch page UI in the same PR as the wire plumbing, fully satisfying the literal "UI" half of item 2 for both fields at once.
- **Tradeoff**: A1 is smaller, lower-risk, ships the actual dogfooding capability (SD receiving opencode dispatches from Harbour) fastest, and is consistent with how `model` itself was rolled out. A2 fully closes out item 2's UI language in one shot but meaningfully widens the diff (new UI state, wiring into `public/dispatch.js`'s send handler, styling, plus now TWO new UI controls instead of zero) for a page that has apparently not needed a model control to be useful so far. **This is a real fork — beat 4 should pick one explicitly, not default into it.**

**Fork B: how to add `harness` validation given the discovered `model` divergence bug.**
- *Option B1 — extract a shared validator.* Pull the duplicated opaque-string checks (length + `DANGEROUS_CHARS_REGEX`) that `routes/proxy.js` and `routes/dispatch.js` both hand-roll into one shared helper (there is currently no shared validation module between the two routers — each inlines its own `MAX_NAME_LENGTH`/`DANGEROUS_CHARS_REGEX` checks), used for both `model` and the new `harness`. This would fix the beat-2-discovered divergence (`model: 0` rejected by `routes/proxy.js:4242` but silently accepted by `routes/dispatch.js:310`) as a side effect of adding `harness` correctly the first time.
- *Option B2 — mirror today's pattern faithfully.* Write `harness` validation independently in each router, matching the existing (divergent) style of each file, and deliberately leave the pre-existing `model` divergence untouched as an out-of-scope pre-existing bug (candidate for its own separate ticket).

## Beat 4/4 — Final implementation plan

See beats 1-3 (comments above) for the full evidence trail; this beat decides the two open forks and assembles the concrete plan. Full plan also copied into the issue description under **## Implementation Plan**.

### Fork decisions

**Fork A: API/proxy-only now (A1), UI deferred.** `model` shipped with zero Dispatch-page UI exposure for its entire life (LIN-438) without that being treated as a gap, and the ticket's own wording ("UI **and/or** API/automation surface") treats these as alternatives, not a mandatory pair. Wiring `harness` through the API/proxy layer alone unblocks the actual driving use case (an orchestrator or automation dispatching an opencode task) at a fraction of the diff size and risk. UI selector is a well-scoped, separate follow-up ticket.

**Fork B: extract a shared validator (B1).** The beat-2-discovered divergence (`routes/proxy.js:4242` rejects `model: 0`, `routes/dispatch.js:310` silently accepts it) proves the duplicate-and-hope pattern already drifts; adding a second field (`harness`) via the same duplicated-by-hand pattern doubles that risk instead of fixing it. A small shared validator used by both routers for both fields costs little extra and removes the recurring failure mode outright.

### Implementation plan (file-by-file, in order)

**1. Shared validator (new, small) — `lib/dispatch-validation.js`**
- Export `validateOpaqueDispatchField(value, fieldName, { maxLength = MAX_NAME_LENGTH })` — the type/length/`DANGEROUS_CHARS_REGEX` check currently duplicated (with the discovered drift) at `routes/proxy.js:4242-4266` and `routes/dispatch.js:305-331`. Returns `{ error }` or `null`.
- No behavior change to `model`'s validation semantics beyond fixing the `0`-vs-falsy drift to match the stricter (`proxy.js`) form — call this out in the PR description since it's a (tiny, correctness) behavior change to existing `model` validation, not just new `harness` code.

**2. Store layer — `lib/dispatch-store.js` (the load-bearing seam; do this before the routers so both routers forward into a store that already accepts the field)**
- `addItem` (`:138`, JSDoc `:126`): add `@param {string} [item.harness]` JSDoc entry; store `harness: item.harness || null` beside `model: item.model || null` (`:171`).
- `_formatItem` (`:948`): add `harness: doc.harness || null` beside `model: doc.model || null` (`:969`) — this is the line the external runner's poll/take read actually depends on.
- Archive/history path (`:517`): add `harness: doc.harness || null` beside the existing `model: doc.model || null`.
- Add a top-of-file schema-comment entry mirroring the existing `model` line (`:21`).

**3. Proxy router — `routes/proxy.js`**
- `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` (`:4135`): destructure `harness` at `:4142`; validate via the new shared helper (replacing the inline `model` checks at `:4242-4266` with calls to the same helper, for both fields); forward `harness: harness || null` beside `:4394`.
- `POST /api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` (`:4451`): destructure at `:4451`; validate `:4493-4498` via the shared helper; forward at **both** call sites, `:4600` and `:4741` — beat 2 flagged this as the easiest place to miss one of two call sites.
- `formatDispatchWatch` (`:445-478`, the `GET /dispatch/{id}` watch response): note this function does **not** echo `model` today either — leave `harness` out of it too for consistency (not a new gap, matches existing `model` behavior; do not silently "fix" this as scope creep).
- Update the embedded `/api/proxy/instructions` text (`:1240-1257`) to document `harness` alongside `model` on both endpoints.
- **Wording fix (beat 3)**: `:1272` — replace the literal "cold claude --resume" with generic phrasing (e.g. "a cold resume via the runner's own mechanism").

**4. User dispatch router — `routes/dispatch.js`**
- `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` (`:199`): destructure `harness` at `:199`; validate via the shared helper (replacing `:305-331`); forward at `:413`.

**5. Docs — `docs/dispatch-integration.md`**
- Add a `harness` row to the field table (`:279`) and a new "Harness (`harness`)" section mirroring "Execution model (`model`)" (`:499-533`) — document it as opaque, forwarded blindly, SD-default-preserving on `null`/omit, and explicitly note (per the ticket's precedence constraint) that Harbour does NOT interpose a per-workspace default — payload value or omit, nothing in between (per beat 2's finding: `resolveWorkspaceModel` is a different, generation-model namespace and is NOT reused here).

**6. Deferred (separate follow-up ticket, not this pass): Dispatch-page UI control.** `public/dispatch.js` + `lib/render-dispatch.js` get a harness dropdown + model input only in that follow-up, per the Fork A decision.

### Dependency order

Store (`lib/dispatch-store.js`) has no dependency on the routers and should land first, since both routers forward into it — landing the routers first would mean forwarding into a store that silently drops the field. Shared validator can land alongside or just before the store (no runtime dependency between them). Both routers depend on the shared validator + the store change. Docs depend on the routers being finalized (so the documented shape matches reality). Order: **validator → store → proxy router → user-dispatch router → docs**.
